title: Register the PIM Manager licence
purpose: Registers an issued PIM Manager licence in the environment's store: it verifies the signed licence document first, stores it as the License setting, reads it back and verifies it again; optionally stores the Invardia install key or queues its claim.
whenToRun: When a licence file has been issued (a new Pro licence, a renewal or a replacement) and it cannot be registered in PIM Manager itself (Settings > Licence, SuperAdmin). The licence page shows this command with the environment's server and tenant filled in. The installer runs it for you.

runAs.name: Member of the environment's SQL admin group (grp-pim-sql-admins), signed in with az login
runAs.why: The licence is kept in pim.Settings; only the SQL admin group may write it. With -UseSignedInAccount the signed-in az user is used (the recommended way). Alternatively an Azure SQL access token (-SqlAccessToken), the admin application (-AdminAppId with -AdminCertThumbprint), or a ready -ConnectionString to a local SQL Server.

changes.object: pim.Settings row 'License' (the signed licence document exactly as issued)
changes.scope: this environment's PIM Manager and engine
changes.why: Switches on the features the licence covers. The document is verified BEFORE the store is written (a tampered or foreign-signed document, a non-Pro licence or one not bound to this tenant is refused), then read back and verified again.
changes.undo: Register the previous licence file again (the replaced licence id is printed as 'replaces:'), or remove the License setting to return to Community.

changes.object: pim.Settings row 'EditionUpgrade' (only when the environment was Community until now)
changes.why: Records the Community-to-Pro conversion so the update ring keeps working until the upgrade step gives the environment its Pro updater.
Stores the install key Invardia issued with this installation so the engine does not claim another one. The key is never printed.
changes.undo: Remove the two settings; the engine's install-key job then claims a key again.

changes.object: pim.Settings row 'SchedulerTriggers' (adds one 'install-key' run-now entry) -- only with -QueueInstallKeyClaim and no key given
changes.why: So the engine claims the install key at its next run (within 5 minutes) instead of up to 6 hours later.
changes.undo: None needed -- the entry is consumed by the next engine run.

changes.object: the result file named by -OutFile (licence id, status, features; never the install key)
changes.why: For a caller that reads the outcome.

parameters.name: LicensePath
parameters.help: The issued licence file (.pimlicense / .aitlicense). Its content is imported; the file is not kept. Give this or -LicenseJson.

parameters.name: LicenseJson
parameters.help: The issued licence document as text, instead of -LicensePath.

parameters.name: ConnectionString
parameters.help: A ready connection string to the store (e.g. a local SQL Server) instead of -SqlServer.

parameters.name: SqlServer
parameters.help: The store's server (alias -SqlServerFqdn). An Azure SQL FQDN connects with a token.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The tenant id; required for an Azure SQL store. The licence must name this tenant.

parameters.name: UseSignedInAccount
parameters.help: Reach the store as the signed-in az user (a member of the SQL admin group). The recommended way.

parameters.name: SqlAccessToken
parameters.help: Automation: an Azure SQL access token the caller already holds; the machine's managed identity is never used.

parameters.name: AdminAppId
parameters.help: Automation: the admin application's client id (with -AdminCertThumbprint or -AdminSecret).

parameters.name: AdminCertThumbprint
parameters.help: Automation: the thumbprint of the admin application's certificate in the local machine store.

parameters.name: AdminSecret
parameters.help: Legacy automation only: a client secret for -AdminAppId. Not for customer use; prefer -UseSignedInAccount.

parameters.name: InstallKey
parameters.help: The install key Invardia issued with this installation (inv-...). Stored, never printed.

parameters.name: InstallKeyPath
parameters.help: The install key in a file (so it is never a command-line argument); the claim state is recorded as 'claimed'.

parameters.name: QueueInstallKeyClaim
parameters.help: With no key given: queue the engine's install-key claim for its next run.

parameters.name: RequireMspRole
parameters.help: 'Master' or 'Slave' (managing / managed tenant): refuse, before storing, a licence that does not cover MSP for this tenant.

parameters.name: OutFile
parameters.help: Write the outcome as JSON to this file.

readsOnly: the licence file named by -LicensePath (and the key file named by -InstallKeyPath)
pim.Settings 'License' (what is stored now, to report the licence it replaces; a store that cannot be read is not written)
pim.Settings 'SchedulerTriggers' (only with -QueueInstallKeyClaim, so an install-key entry is not added twice)
whatIf: Verifies the licence document, reads what is stored now and prints the licence (id, customer, SKU, valid to, features, bound tenants, what it replaces), 'What if: Performing the operation "store the verified licence" on target "pim.Settings['License'] in <server>/<database>"' and 'What if: would store licence <id> ...' (plus the install key or its claim when asked). Nothing is written.
undo: Register the previous licence file again (its id is printed as 'replaces:'), or remove the License setting to return the environment to Community. Remove InvardiaInstallKey / InstallKeyClaimState to have the engine claim a key again.
